newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Platinum leads precious metals higher in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Platinum leads precious metals higher in Europe.

text.p: Platinum led precious metals higher in nervous European trading on Monday as concern about Russian supplies continued to support the market, dealers said.
"It is the same story with the Russians," one dealer at a Swiss bank said, suggesting platinum would move towards resistance at $385 an ounce and palladium might advance toward $160/$161.
Platinum started at $380.00/$381.00 versus $377.50/$378.50 at the London close on Friday, while palladium gained $3.75 an ounce to $156.00/$157.00.
But both metals remained vulnerable to fresh news that might turn the market.
Gold started at $342.50/$343.00, marginally higher than Friday's close at $342.20/$342.70, but traders said gold's room to rise was limited and predicted it would move in a narrow range.
Silver was steady at $4.75/$4.77. Traders saw support around $4.74 and resistance between $4.85 and $4.90.
Trading in Zurich was expected to be thin because of a local holiday.
